To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

RLP-C and CVD risk in women: 1) are associated, 2) are independent of each other and of other major risk factors, 3) are more strongly associated than are TGs and CVD risk, and 4) are more strongly predictive of CVD events in women than are other lipids
remnant-like particle (rlp) cholesterol is a new, independent cardiovascular disease risk marker in women.
RLP-C, an assay for remnant-like particles, is an independent risk marker for cardiovascular disease in women.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of the molecular mechanisms underlying the pathogenesis of the metabolic syndrome and its complications in humans.
the role of remnants of chylomicron and very low density lipoprotein in the development of atherosclerosis and cardiovascular disease.

the development of a new method for the measurement of remnant-like cholesterol (RLP cholesterol) and remnant-like triglyceride (TRL cholesterol) in human plasma, the application of this method for the study of remnant lipids in human populations, and the evaluation of the role of RLP cholesterol as an independent cardiovascular risk factor in women.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
RLP-C, an independent risk factor in women, is an important new marker for cardiovascular disease.
RLP-C (but not RLP-TG) is a risk factor for CAVD in women.
RLP-C and triglycerides are important independent risk factors for CVD in both men and women.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
RLP-C, a marker of the metabolic syndrome, is a risk factor for CVC in women.
the presence of RLP-C is a risk factor for CVA and MI in women.
remnant-like particle cholesterol is an independent risk marker for cardiovascular disease in women, and that this assay provides more information than do other lipids and lipoproteins.
The main takeaway from our work is that
RLP-C and triglycerides provide independent information regarding CVD in women.
RLP-C and triglycerides are not interchangeable and that RLP-C should be used in the assessment of cardiovascular disease risk.
remnant lipoprotein cholesterol is a strong independent cardiovascular disease risk predictor in women.
